summary: The Fulbright Foreign Student Program, sponsored by the US government, brings graduate students, young professionals and artists from more than 160 countries to study in the United States. You apply in your home country, through its Fulbright Commission or the US Embassy.
covers: A monthly stipend for housing and living costs, and health insurance.
Travel to and from the United States.
Tuition: many host universities give full or partial tuition waivers to Fulbright students; what your grant covers depends on your country's programme.
About 4,000 foreign students receive Fulbright grants each year.
eligibility: Citizens of a participating country, applying through that country's Fulbright Commission/Foundation or US Embassy.
Usually a completed bachelor's degree and strong English; many countries also want work or leadership experience.
Each country sets its own eligible fields, levels (master's, PhD, research) and requirements.
how_to_apply: Find the Fulbright page for your country (through the Commission or the US Embassy website).
Read that country's call — deadline, documents, tests and fields.
Submit the application, usually 15 to 18 months before you would start in the US.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed; the Fulbright system then places you at, or confirms, a US university.
watch_out: There is no single global deadline — each country sets its own, often between February and October.
Many countries require you to return home after the grant (the J-1 two-year home residency rule applies to most Fulbrighters).
Fulbright never charges an application fee through agents; apply only through the official Commission or Embassy.
